paragraphs: 1. What is unique about the home of the Khasi people?
a. Their ancestral home spans the border of India and Bangladesh.
b. The trees in their native land are particularly long-lived, with many surviving for hundreds of years.
c. It receives more rainfall than any place on earth.
d. The terrain is mountainous with many narrow river gorges.
2. How long does it take to “grow” a living bridge?
a. According to the Watson, it takes 75 years for the bridge to grow.
b. Watson reports that the bridges take 50 years to grow.
c. The video says that bridges can be completed in as little as two weeks.
d. The video claims that it takes centuries for these bridges to develop.
3. Why have we not heard about many of the cultures Watson cites in the video?
a. Many of these cultures are marginalized by dominant cultures.
b. The cultures are secretive and do not seek attention.
c. Most of these places do not have advanced technology like television, phone service, and internet.
d. These cultures have evolved in some of the most remote and extreme environments on earth.
4. Watson reports that the Ma’dan people use reeds for many things. Which of the following is NOT listed as a use for the reeds?
a. Construction material.
b. Food for humans.
c. Animal feed.
d. Medicine.
e. The Ma’dan use reeds for ALL of the above.
f. The Ma’dan use reeds for NONE of the above.
5. How long will the floating islands of the Ma’dan people float?
a. The islands will float for more than twenty-five years.
b. The islands will float for generations.
c. The islands will float for thousands of years.
d. The video does not say for how long the islands will float.
6. According to Julia Watson, what happens when people rush to the future?
a. People often miss obvious solutions to problems.
b. People overlook solutions that people invented in the past.
c. People make the same mistakes over and over again.
d. People look back and romanticize the past.
7. The video describes many unusual features of Calcutta’s wastewater treatment system. Which feature is most
unusual?
a. The system operates entirely without electricity.
b. The system relies on sunlight to purify the water.
c. The treatment takes only a few days.
d. The treatment process produces fish that is sold in local markets.
8. While other cities are now emulating Calcutta’s wastewater treatment system, what is Calcutta doing?
a. Calcutta is actively developing its floodplain.
b. Calcutta is patenting their wastewater treatment system and selling plans to other cities.
c. Calcutta is struggling to save its floodplains from development.
d. Calcutta is busy building a modern wastewater treatment plant.
9. How long does it take for Calcutta to convert wastewater to clean water?
a. The process takes seven days.
b. The process takes thirty days.
c. The process takes six months.
d. The process takes about one year.
10. What does the word “ganvie” mean?
a. It means “house on legs.”
b. It means “big lake.”
c. It means “we survive.”
d. The video does not say what “ganvie” means.
11. Which of the following is NOT found among the Tofinu people?
a. A bank.
b. Bars.
c. A mosque.
d. A post office.
e. All of the above are found.
f. None of the above are found.
12. What is the greatest threat to the world’s mangrove ecosystems?
a. Industrial pollution.
b. Overfishing.
c. Fish farms.
d. Global warming.
13. What was surprising about indigenous fire-stick farming?
a. The amount of food that the aborigines produce is astonishing.
b. That the natives were able to farm such harsh land at all is astonishing.
c. It is surprising that other Australians didn’t adapt the practice sooner.
d. The native farms survived the wildfires.
14. What does Julia Watson find surprising about ancient technologies?
a. Watson is intrigued by these technologies because they are so attuned to nature.
b. Watson reports that these technologies are so complex that we might not be able to use them today.
c. Watson finds it fascinating that these ancient technologies are so inexpensive.
d. Watson is astounded that these technologies have survived for thousands of years.
15. According to Watson, what do people do with concrete, steel, and glass?
a. People use these materials to build the technologies that advance our civilization.
b. People use these to build fortresses.
c. People use building materials to fight against nature.
d. People use these materials to solve the problems threatening our existence.
16. What does Julia Watson do for a living?
a. She is a university professor.
b. She is an architect.
c. She is a reporter.
d. The video does not say what Watson does for a living.
